newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty straddles parity rate, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Zloty straddles parity rate, seen stable.

text.p: The Polish zloty eased in early trade to straddle the parity rate and dealers said the market was likely to stay at the trading band centre for the day.

They said players were quoting large spreads, on the one hand wary of a central bank intervention in support of the zloty if the unit eased too much and on the other hand fearing large zloty-sell orders from abroad if the currency firmed.

"The market lacks a clear trend and is likely to keep around the band centre to avoid a large zloty sell order and a potential central bank intervention," said Rafal Kaminski, forex dealer at Pekao SA.

At 0835 GMT the zloty moved to 0.03/0.20 below parity against 0.19/0.03 percent above parity at the opening. It was at 3.3520/610 against the dollar and 1.8795/840 against the mark, down from 3.3390/440 and 1.8790/825 respectively.
"Foreigners keep selling small amount of Polish T-bills but they are doing it gently," said Artur Wrobel, T-bill and bond dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.

Dealers said the prime minister's Sunday remarks that the government may ask for increased borrowing in the central bank to help those affected by floods in southern Poland, so far seemed to have no effect on the market.

On the money market O/N and T/N rates eased on a net inflow of 1.309 billion zlotys into the system after the National Bank of Poland said it would not stage any open market operations on Monday. T-bill yields are expected to rise at the 800 million zloty primary tender today on low demand.
The benchmark 52-week T-bill yield is seen rising to 22.1 percent from last week's 21.86 after NBP-bill yields increased by about 0.3 point to 22.50 percent last week.
Dealers said the 26-week and 13-week T-bill yield should rise by about 0.1 to 0.15 point from the previous 21.71 and 21.13 percent. -- Jan Strupczewski +48 22 653 9700
